## 2026-10-29 progress: 13 -> 10, and what the last 10 need

**Done: the 2 strays (MISSING_CREATE x2 + FOREIGN_STORE_PATH).** `1022-d72f-4b89-49a3` and `af41-7784-737d-43e1` held only a gitignored `.cache.json` each (mtime 2026-09-12 22:23 PDT). They are the two planning tickets removed in the 2026-09-12 redaction: their CREATE commits are reachable only from `refs/tags/backup/tickets-pre-redaction`, and their original CREATE events are in the operator's local-only archive. The caches were copied there (sha256 verified), then removed with `rebar store maintenance --clean` (no --force; 0 unpushed commits). Backup ref `refs/rebar-maintenance/20261029T090716Z`, audit in the tracker gitdir.

**Remaining, none fixable by repair alone:**

1. **UNSIGNED_ENV (492a5c71, this operator host).** No signing identity exists here: no `.rebar/current_identity`, no `identity.signing_key`, no `REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY`, no SSH key in `~/.ssh`. Setting one up means choosing/creating key material and registering a public key in the shared store (docs/identity-setup.md). Past unsigned events stay unsigned; the finding stops only for new writes.
2. **ENV_ID_MISMATCH (492a5c71 vs ade0f2ef, b8a354e0).** `env_identity.divergence_report` flags any author seen under more than one env id. Here every clone writes as the shared bot identity (AGENTS.md: shared credentials are a permanent operating constraint), so a healthy multi-clone store matches the "re-clone" signature. The docstring says it fires even for acknowledged changes, and it reads history that is never rewritten, so on this store fsck can never be clean. A fix needs a design choice (e.g. a recorded, store-committed acknowledgement of known sibling env ids).
3. **8 ORPHAN_EVENTs on 6 tickets** (EDIT x4, FILE_IMPACT x2, STATUS, SIGNATURE). The repair classifies these as order-sensitive and leaves them for human triage.

## 2026-10-29: the 8 ORPHAN_EVENTs resolved — fsck now 2 issues (both identity)

Triage, done read-only on an isolated clone before touching the live store: for each of the 6 tickets, reduce from the current SNAPSHOT vs a full-log fold (`fsck_repair.rebuild_source_state`). 79b2, 93e5, e042, f1d6: identical. b4f5: only `parent_status_uuid` (to the orphan STATUS event, the ticket's latest status write) and `status_fork_resolutions`. 1eb6: only the legacy `signature` mirror. Rebuilt all 6 on the clone, then compared before/after: every ticket stays `closed`, `attestations` (completion-verifier, plan-review) identical, and only b4f5's status-chain pointer moves.

A false alarm on the way, recorded so nobody repeats it: comparing the legacy `signature` field shows every rebuilt ticket as "lost". It is not: compaction never persists that mirror (compact_txn `_snapshot_strip_keys`, task 7ed9), ordinarily compacted tickets also replay with `signature: null`, and the real record, `attestations`, is preserved. Checked on the 12 df72 rebuilds too: attestations intact.

Applied to the live store with `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` (6 REBUILD SNAPSHOT commits, pre-run HEAD 08805232e9b), pushed strictly; local == origin. Live fsck: 2 issues, ENV_ID_MISMATCH and UNSIGNED_ENV (see previous comment). 29 at the start of today.

## 2026-11-02: ENV_ID_MISMATCH root cause measured; implementation of option (2) paused for a design input

Reproduced read-only against the live store with `EnvAuthorshipTally` + `env_identity.divergence_report` (the exact fsck path, `fsck_tracker_health._tracker_health`).

**What drives the finding.** `divergence_report` keys authors by the free-text `author` display name. The 3 env ids are sequential, not concurrent: ade0f2ef 2026-06-26..08-09 PDT, b8a354e0 08-09..09-10 PDT, 492a5c71 09-14 PDT..now. The bot's display name on this host is "Rebar Bot Nava"; on the older envs it is "RebarBotNava". Those strings differ, so the bot never overlaps. The only overlapping author is **"Joe Oakhart"**: 8 events on 492a5c71 (09-14..09-20, email joeoakhart@navapbc.com, no author_id) vs 1358 on ade0f2ef and 4549 on b8a354e0 (a mix of the bot email + bot author_id 594c-9dcf-5ad6-4e6d and the human email).

**Consequence for option (2).** Skipping the bot by display name changes nothing on this store. Re-keying by identity (author_id, else email) and skipping identity 594c-9dcf-5ad6-4e6d still leaves joeoakhart@navapbc.com under both 492a5c71 and b8a354e0, so fsck still reports ENV_ID_MISMATCH. Under the decision, other authors keep the check, so that remaining line would need its own justification (AC6) or another decision.

**No existing source names the shared bot identity.** Checked: the `[identity]` config section (only require_authenticated, signing_key, enforce_since), the identity ticket 594c-9dcf-5ad6-4e6d (no tag or field marks it as shared), rebar.toml, and the bot email in source (only `BRIDGE_BOT_EMAIL`, a CI-runner env var read by `_bridge_runner`, not available to fsck on a dev host). Implementing the skip needs a new mechanism, such as a config key or an identity-ticket marker. Per instructions, no code was written; options are reported to the operator.

Worktree `.rebar/worktrees/fix-esok-envid` is provisioned at origin/main b2dca9bf5ea, with no changes.

comments.author: Rebar Bot Nava
comments.body:
## 2026-11-03: live fsck with the overlap rule — 0 issues

Read-only `rebar store fsck --dry-run` against the live tracker (`/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.tickets-tracker`, current env 492a5c71), run from worktree `fix-esok-overlap`.

**Before** (origin/main `f1fe7c6f587`, 09:12 PST): one counted issue.
```
ENV_ID_MISMATCH: this environment ('492a5c71-6cda-48a6-8134-02ff6a672739') has also written events under 2 other environment id(s) (ade0f2ef-51cc-45a2-bb97-c09846cd3df5, b8a354e0-12c3-4cf2-bbf1-fcc9685d5126) — the same author(s) appear under both. ...
fsck complete: 1 issues found      (exit 1)
```

**After** (commit `b6c09c0bfad`-lineage, Gerrit change 3270 patch set 1, 09:29 PST): no `ENV_ID_MISMATCH` line (grep count 0). Tail:
```
ensures: 10/10 applied
authorship: 60117 signed, 20254 unsigned event(s) — run `rebar verify-identity`
fsck complete: no issues found      (exit 0)
```
No `UNSIGNED_ENV`, `FOREIGN_STORE_PATH`, `MISSING_CREATE`, `ORPHAN_EVENT` or `SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT` lines in either run. Lines that remain are informational and not counted (`UNCERTIFIED_CLOSE`, `STATUS_FORK_RESOLVED`).

**Overlap rule.** Closed intervals: per author, the spans `(first, last)` under two env ids overlap when `a1 <= b2 and a2 <= b1`. A shared boundary timestamp counts as overlap, and a span with no integer timestamp counts as overlapping. On this store's Aug 9 handover, RebarBotNava's last event under ade0f2ef (19:51:58.58 PDT) and first under b8a354e0 (20:44:59.12 PDT) are 53 minutes apart, so the rule classifies them as sequential. A test pins those exact timestamps.

**Stated limit.** Event timestamps are HLC values (`hlc.next_tick` = max(cache, ticket witness, wall clock)+1). They are never earlier than the writer's wall clock but can run later. Cross-host clock skew larger than the gap between two clones can therefore misclassify them in either direction. This is documented in `_overlaps`.

Discovered and filed: westbound-chivalric-pinemarten. The ENV_ID_MISMATCH line and the mint warning both still say re-clone attestations stop verifying, which has been false by default since `3bde5613718` (bug `c21f-6f29-5d2d-4a5a`).

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

`rebar store fsck` on the live tickets store started at 99 issues across 4 classes (2026-10-28). Repairs recorded in this ticket's comments (2026-10-29 and 2026-11-02) cleared the strays, the orphaned/snapshot events and `UNSIGNED_ENV`. A read-only `rebar store fsck --dry-run` from a worktree at `f1fe7c6f587` on 2026-11-03 now counts exactly **1** issue:

```
ENV_ID_MISMATCH: this environment ('492a5c71-…') has also written events under 2 other environment id(s) (ade0f2ef-…, b8a354e0-…) — the same author(s) appear under both. …
fsck complete: 1 issues found
```

`env_identity.divergence_report` (`src/rebar/_store/env_identity.py:221`) reports every other env id that shares a display name with the current env. The only shared name is "Joe Oakhart", and its writes under each env are disjoint in time (measured 2026-11-03 from the live store's event files, PDT):

| env | Joe Oakhart's first event | last event |
|---|---|---|
| ade0f2ef | 2026-07-13 15:59:59 | 2026-07-23 10:22:52 |
| b8a354e0 | 2026-08-22 18:21:22 | 2026-08-24 03:11:42 |
| 492a5c71 (current) | 2026-09-14 22:09:58 | 2026-09-20 01:46:29 |

These are successive re-clones, so fsck can never report 0.

## Decision (operator, 2026-11-03)

Treat env ids whose event time ranges do not overlap as successive re-clones of one store and do not report them. Supersedes the 2026-11-02 "skip the shared bot" choice. Accepted trade-off: fsck no longer flags a clone that was retired and then replaced. No new config key and no identity marker. Authors stay matched by display name.

## Approach

1. `EnvAuthorshipTally` (`src/rebar/_commands/fsck_authorship.py`) already sees every event's `env_id`, `author` and `timestamp` in fsck's single pass (`fsck_scan._check_json_validity`). Replace its per-env author set with a per-author `(first, last)` span of integer event timestamps, and replace `identity_pairs()` with `identity_spans()` returning `{(env_id, author): (first, last) | None}`. `None` means no event for that pair carried an integer timestamp.
2. `divergence_report(current, spans)` reports a foreign env only when some author shared with `current` has overlapping spans under both. Overlap uses **closed** intervals: spans `(a1, b1)` and `(a2, b2)` overlap when `a1 <= b2 and a2 <= b1`. Equal timestamps therefore count as overlap. A successor's first write must come strictly after its predecessor's last write, so a shared nanosecond timestamp cannot come from succession. A pair with no timestamp (`None`) counts as overlapping: its order cannot be established, so it keeps the earlier behaviour.
3. Rule checked against the live Aug 9 handover: "RebarBotNava" last wrote under ade0f2ef at 2026-08-09 19:51:58.58 PDT and first wrote under b8a354e0 at 20:44:59.12 PDT, a 53-minute gap. The rule classifies that as sequential.
4. `fsck_tracker_health._tracker_health` passes `identity_spans()` instead of `identity_pairs()`. The finding text says the same author wrote under both env ids during overlapping periods.
5. Update `docs/concurrency.md` §ENV_ID_MISMATCH to state the overlap scoping and the accepted trade-off.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_store/env_identity.py`: `divergence_report` and an `_overlaps` helper.
- `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_authorship.py`: per-author spans, `identity_spans()`.
- `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_tracker_health.py`: call site.
- `tests/interfaces/store/test_env_identity_guard.py`: the re-clone fixture must now interleave writes, plus new overlap cases.
- `docs/concurrency.md`: detector description.

Out of scope: matching by identity instead of display name. Also out of scope: the stale attestation sentence in the finding text (tracked as its own bug).

## Testing

Tests first, seen failing; no autouse fixtures.

- Sequential spans for one author under two env ids: `divergence_report` returns `None`.
- Overlapping spans: reported, naming the foreign env.
- Boundary: the foreign env's last timestamp equals the current env's first timestamp. This is reported, per the closed-interval rule.
- The live Aug 9 handover timestamps are classified as sequential.
- A pair with no timestamp is still reported.
- A different author's overlap does not count. That keeps the multi-clone boundary.
- `EnvAuthorshipTally.identity_spans()` records min/max per (env, author), skips snapshots, and ignores non-integer timestamps.
- End to end through `fsck_cli`: the existing `test_fsck_reports_env_id_divergence` and `test_fsck_json_carries_the_finding` use a fixture whose foreign-env writes interleave in time with the current env. A new case shows that a purely sequential re-clone exits 0 with no `ENV_ID_MISMATCH`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [non-codebase] `UNSIGNED_ENV` root cause established and remedied: this host had no signing identity; it now signs as the bot identity (comments 2026-10-29, 2026-11-02), and the 2026-11-03 live fsck shows no `UNSIGNED_ENV` line.
  provenance: environment=live tickets store on the operator host; principal=RebarBotNava; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — read-only `rebar store fsck --dry-run` against the live tracker
- [ ] [non-codebase] `ENV_ID_MISMATCH` root cause established: display-name matching across 3 sequential env ids, with "Joe Oakhart" the only shared author (comment 2026-11-02; spans in the table above).
  provenance: environment=live tickets store on the operator host; principal=RebarBotNava; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — read-only scan of the live store's event files
- [ ] [non-codebase] The 2 `FOREIGN_STORE_PATH` strays were removed with `rebar store maintenance --clean` and 8 `ORPHAN_EVENT`s were rebuilt from the full log (comments 2026-10-29); the 2026-11-03 live fsck shows none of `FOREIGN_STORE_PATH`, `MISSING_CREATE`, `ORPHAN_EVENT`, `SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT`.
  provenance: environment=live tickets store on the operator host; principal=RebarBotNava; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — read-only `rebar store fsck --dry-run` against the live tracker
- [ ] The re-clone remedy (carry over `.env-id`, `.opcert-key`, `.opcert-key.pub`, `.ensure-applied`) stays documented in `docs/concurrency.md` and in the mint warning (`env_identity.reidentification_warning`), and `docs/concurrency.md` describes the overlap scoping and its trade-off.
- [ ] Loud unsigned writes stay enforced: `pytest tests/unit/test_unsigned_env_fsck.py` passes.
- [ ] `divergence_report` reports a foreign env only for a shared author with overlapping closed-interval spans. Proved by new tests in `tests/interfaces/store/test_env_identity_guard.py` (sequential → `None`; overlapping → reported; equal boundary timestamp → reported; Aug 9 handover → `None`; no-timestamp pair → reported; other author's overlap → `None`). Each test is seen failing before the change.
- [ ] `pytest tests/interfaces/store/test_env_identity_guard.py tests/unit/test_unsigned_env_fsck.py tests/unit/test_scan_scoping.py` passes, and `make lint` and `make typecheck` exit 0 with the worktree `.venv/bin` first on PATH.
- [ ] [non-codebase] With the new code, a read-only `rebar store fsck --dry-run` against the live tracker prints no `ENV_ID_MISMATCH` line, ends `fsck complete: no issues found` and exits 0; the output tail is recorded in a ticket comment.
  provenance: environment=live tickets store on the operator host; principal=RebarBotNava; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — read-only fsck run from the change's worktree
- [ ] [non-codebase] The change lands through Gerrit with `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`; the change number and merged SHA are recorded in a ticket comment.
  provenance: environment=rebar.solutions.navateam.com Gerrit; principal=RebarBotNava; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — Gerrit change detail with DETAILED_LABELS
